recap.description: Two or three short sentences to the user (≤300 chars): what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified. Its first sentence is the sidebar status. It must stand on its own, since it is also read away from the transcript and the box draws under anything you write after this call: never point at anything else in the conversation ("listed below", "see above", "in my message").

blocked.description: true when your work stops here until the user answers (the app marks the session as waiting on them); omit when the answer can wait.

action.description: An app action update_plan's result listed as available now, or one your own work this turn made available; anything else is refused, and one that stops being available later is dropped (as actions[0], with your ask and the other answers), so do not guess. Omit for a reply.

label.description: For a reply: the button text, 1–3 words (4 only when three cannot say it) / 24 characters — "Yes, fix 1", "Fix 2 instead", "Not now": a button, not a sentence. A click sends it to you as the user's answer. No leading / or !. Ignored for an app action (the app's own label is used).

They are answers to your ask: the first accepts your recommendation, and another is there only when it is a realistic alternative the user might pick instead — not a menu of everything you mentioned. tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

input.description: That tool's input — same shape you'd pass when calling it directly. For computer items whose action is left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key or type, and for form_input items, include action_summary in the item's input, as you would when calling that tool directly.

actions.description: List of tool calls to execute sequentially. Example: [{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"left_click","ref":"ref_12"}},{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"type","text":"hello"}},{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"screenshot"}}]

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'press_key' presses a hardware key 'count' times: return, delete (backspace), an arrow, select_all, undo or redo (a key also hides the on-screen keyboard); 'set_appearance' switches the device to light or dark mode; 'appearance' says which it is in; 'set_keyboard' shows or hides the on-screen keyboard (it appears only while a text field has focus, and 'press_key' and 'text' hide it again); 'rotate' turns the device a quarter turn left or right ('direction'); take a 'screenshot' after it and tap in that screenshot's frame, however it comes back; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': absolute path (no ~) to the built .app bundle (e.g. /Users/me/Library/Developer/Xcode/DerivedData/MyApp-abc123/Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the simulator already attached, else the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

key.description: For 'press_key': the key or edit command to press.

count.description: For 'press_key': how many times to press it, 1 to 20 (default 1).

state.description: For 'set_keyboard': 'show' or 'hide' the on-screen keyboard. For 'set_appearance': 'light' or 'dark'.

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

Use 1 for simple visuals, more for complex ones. - The frozen spec specs/ERN_Memory_Model_Specification_v0.md is the only semantic source. Cite clauses as §N or §N.k (item k).
- Formalize each clause as written. Never add a clause the text does not state (no "robustness"); never drop one.
- When a clause has no checkable content in the state (undefined term), do not invent content: omit it from the definition and record it in readings.md (clause, quote, why it cannot be formalized).
- When a clause has two readings, use the one listed below; if the case is not listed, use the draft's reading if the draft matches one of the readings, and record it in readings.md with both readings and an example of a program whose verdict changes.
- A representation choice that changes no accepted program is free (record it briefly).

State (§38): S3 = (F, nF, P, I, A, D, dead, pin). No arena registry, no callParams, no freed. Library state lives elsewhere.
Outcomes (§58): one type Outcome3 σ := ok σ | reject | fail; every O1–O16 relation except alloc never yields fail.
O1 derive (§60): takes a region (List Nat, read extensionally), not a place. Preconditions: active source; ExercisableAt source mode; every leaf of region exists, is a leaf, belongs to afp source; mode ≤ effective mode of source on each leaf; §60.3 as a decidable clause (no unrelated active authority becomes incompatible); §60.4 current frame live. §60.1c "origin chain and anchors valid" and §60.4b "footprint and anchoring restrictions": no checkable content -> omitted, recorded.
O2 split (§61): draft clauses (incl. no exclusive right already distributed). §61.4 is NOT a precondition (the §61 note says an accepted split may violate I1 without DDSound) -> recorded.
O3 release (§62): draft clauses; §62.5 (abstraction contracts) omitted, recorded.
O4 transfer (§63): draft clauses MINUS the draft's extra clause "(transferEff s src dst).Usable dst" (not in §63); PLUS §63.8 (local self-blocking prevention, as LockOptions.Opt2Transfer on formal/derivability_0.1); effect: dependencies follow the corresponding places corr(r) (not all to the destination root); §63.6 over moved usable places and AnchorOrder in the resulting state; §63.7 AnchorOrderHeld for the moved held authorities in the resulting state; §63.4 = draft ActiveDerivedOutside reading (recorded); §63.2 child order = place index order (recorded).
O5 depend (§64): draft clauses; §64.2b "real dependency" omitted, recorded.
O8 store (§65): draft clauses (they match).
O9/O10/O11 (§66–§68): add "every leaf belongs to a usable place" (§66.1, §67.1, §68.1); O10 keeps §67.2 explicitly.
O12 endUse (§69): death markers transitive over owned storage; drop the draft's extra disjunct that blocks descendants of authorities the step releases (not in §69.2) -> record the consequence.
O13 free (§70): death markers transitive; no extra "Usable p" and no clearing of D beyond what §70 prescribes; §70.4 scope = the released unit (place and storage that dies with it).
O14 alloc (§71): shape nonempty with exactly ONE root (one new storage root), parts' parents inside the shape, no owner component; provider clause as written in §71.2 (Modify OR writeShared over SharedMutable metadata) -> conflict with §36 recorded; outcomes reject / fail (not Satisfiable) / ok.
O6 enterFrame (§72): locals owned directly by the new frame (no local owned by another local); §72.3 ParamOriginHidden; §72.4 AnchorOrderHeld in the resulting state.
O7 exitFrame (§73): draft (first surviving active origin, held by a frame or a usable place).
O15/O16 pin/unpin (§74, §75): per-leaf dynamic pin flags (draft); unpin requires the place usable and K.ExternalDone(place) on the place; StaticPinnedBottom is a condition on (K, statics), not on states.
HasRight / ExercisableAt (§43): one authority exercisable at m with sufficient effective mode on every leaf (∃ a, ∀ l) as the draft -> recorded.
WF3 (§49): a structure with eight named fields, one per item:
 1 frames: F nonempty, no duplicates, every frame < nF;
 2 places: parent links valid and acyclic (representation: parent index < child index), parts share the owner and death marker of their parent;
 3 owners: owner frames < nF, owner places exist; "well-founded ownership chains reaching a live frame for every usable place" read as stated for usable places (Usable is inductive) -> recorded with the global-acyclicity alternative;
 4 footprints: every footprint member is an existing leaf;
 5 authorities: origins exist and precede (origin index < id: representation of acyclic chains ending at a root);
 6 RootChain (draft);
 7 RootHeld as §49.7 states it: every usable root place has an active root authority, Modify, no origin, held by its owner, whose footprint is the place's footprint (draft RootLive + mode);
 8 holder validity (draft poss).
 The draft's converse RootHeld (every origin-less authority covering a leaf of root r is held by r's owner) is NOT a WF3 clause: keep it as a separate auxiliary predicate.
I2 (§51): mode conservation unconditional (not under ∀ p ∈ footprint).
Initial state (§47): base frame 0; statics may be owned by statics; root authority held by the owner. Well-formedness of the statics declaration (acyclic ownership, parents before children) is not stated by §47: keep the draft ShapeOK-style hypothesis as a hypothesis of the init theorems and record it as a spec gap.
Reachable: closure of S3.init statics under the kernel steps O1–O16 only.

# Readings — handlepool (`formal/Ern/Lib/HandlePool.lean`, non-normative library instance)

Contract: "HandlePool v0.4 annex" (Annex D, items D.1–D.4, of `ERN_MM-03.3_v0.4_pour_validation.md`),
corrected by spec v0 §36 (MetaRight = exercisable `Modify` on the pool value, no `writeShared` branch)
and §56 (guard over all registries of live administrations), and by brief obligation 5.
Spec v0 §75 / Part XIV preamble: the HandlePool contract "belong[s] to [its] library abstraction[s] and
[is] not defined here" (mapping P0). Every definition below that goes beyond §36/§37/§38/§46/§47/§56/
§58/§89 encodes the non-normative contract.

Each entry: clause, quote, reading used, alternative, example whose verdict changes.
Machine-checked witnesses are in the `Witness` namespace of the module (decided by `decide`).

## A. Readings that can change an accepted program (need arbitration)

**H-R1 (mapping P1). Which subplaces are slots.** D.1: "Les slots sont des sous-emplacements deux à
deux disjoints, inclus dans `storage`"; `newPool(storage, internal)` takes no slot description.
Used (draft): the direct children of `storage`, in index order (`kids`), each free, generation 0
(`newPoolEff`). Alternatives: the leaves of `storage`; a slot list passed to `newPool`.
Example: storage `S = {a: {x, y}, b}`: children give slots `a, b` (third `allocSlot` → `fail`);
leaves give `x, y, b` (third `allocSlot` → `ok`). A storage that is a leaf has no slot: every
`allocSlot` gives `fail`.

**H-R2 (mapping P2). `freeSlot` of a free slot whose identity and generation match.** D.3: "un slot
déjà libre n'est pas rendu libérable par cette seule égalité" (excludes `ok`, does not say which
outcome). Used: `fail` (same handle validation `HandleOK` as `resolve`, D.2 "slot … libre ⇒ `fail`").
Alternative: `reject`. Example: fresh pool, `freeSlot(⟨id, 0, 0⟩)` on free slot 0: `fail` (used) vs
`reject`. Theorem `pool_freeSlot_stale_other_free_fails`.

**H-R3 (mapping P3). `resolve`/`resolveMany`/`freeSlot`: right before handle validity.** D.2 orders
handle validation "avant toute création d'autorité", not against the right; §58 "according to the
operation's contract". Used (draft): `reject` without the right (`ResolveRight` = `DerivePre` of the
companion; `AdminRight` for `freeSlot`), then `fail` for an invalid handle. Alternative (§77
analogy): handle `fail` first. Example: with an active `Modify` companion, `resolve(stale h, Modify)`:
`reject` (used) vs `fail`.

**H-R4. Missing pool index.** D.2/D.3 do not say what `resolve`, `resolveMany`, `allocSlot`, `freeSlot`
do on a registry index that names no pool. Used (draft): `reject`. Alternative: `fail`.

**H-R5 (mapping P4). Scope of "excluding `internal` and its ancestors" in `freeSlot`.** D.3: "aucune
autorité active ne couvre l'entrée hors `internal` et ses ancêtres"; brief: "freeSlot ends the entry
content with endUse effects, preconditions excluding internal and its ancestors". Used
(`ContentEndPre`, x exempt iff `x = internal ∨ x ∈ ancs internal`):
- entry: no active authority covers a leaf of the slot place unless exempt (D.3 clause, which also
  subsumes §69.2 on the entry leaves);
- §69.2 on storage that dies with the content (`DyingAccessOK`): **unchanged**, no exemption;
- §69.3 (`ContentAnchorOK`): the exemption removes only the "its root" part (`IsRootOf`) for exempt
  anchors; "held by `place`" and "would become inactive when an owned holder dies" are kept for every
  anchor (they are what keeps I3, §52; an exempt anchor that the effect deactivates would leave a
  usable place with an invalid anchor);
- §69.4 pins: unchanged;
- §69.1 is not a precondition: `freeSlot_modify_right` derives `Usable slot` and
  `HasRight Modify slot` from `AdminRight` + the entry clause on well-formed pools.
Alternatives: (a) exempt `internal`/ancestors in §69.2 also on dying storage; (b) exempt them from
§69.3 entirely. (a) changes no verdict if `internal` and its ancestors never cover storage that dies
with a slot (expected under §49.6 RootChain: one root per covered chain; not proved here). (b) drops
the checks that keep an exempt anchor active: if a usable place depended on `internal` while
`internal` were held within the slot or by a dying holder, the result would violate I3 (§52); whether
such a state also passes the entry clause and `AdminRight` is not settled here, so (b) is not proven
to change a verdict.

**H-R6. `allocSlot` destination right.** D.3 lists "destination utilisable et libre d'autorité active,
non `Init`". Used: also `HasRight Modify dst` (the handle is written into `dst`, an O10 write §67.1;
draft). Alternative: not checked. Example: a destination with only `Observe`: `reject` (used) vs `ok`.

**H-R7. `allocSlot` choice.** D.3: "`ok` choisit un slot libre". Used: relation over any free slot
(mapping R6/B26), not the lowest index. No outcome set is narrowed.

**H-R8. `newPool` obligations taken from `newArena`.** D.1: "Il reprend les autres obligations
applicables de `newArena`". Used: all of §76.1–§76.3 and §76.5 (`Arena.NewArenaBase`), including "all
leaves of the value holding `internal` are `Init`" (draft). Alternative: drop §76.5 as inapplicable.
Example: a pool value with an `Uninit` metadata leaf: `reject` (used) vs `ok`.

**H-R9 (mapping P10). `resolveMany Observe` with an invalid handle.** D.2 states the atomic `fail`
only in the `Modify` sentence. Used: atomic `fail` in both modes (`BatchOK`); distinctness only in
`Modify`. Alternative: no validation in `Observe`. Example: `resolveMany([stale h], Observe)`: `fail`
(used) vs `ok`.

**H-R10. Entry derivations rejected.** The kernel steps of a resolution are checked: if the entry
`derive` (resolve), the `split` (resolveMany Modify) or one of the `Observe` derives (resolveMany
Observe) is not accepted, the outcome is `reject` with no state (atomic). D.2: "Les deux sont soumises
aux règles ordinaires". Alternative: none found.

**H-R11. `unresolve`.** D.2: "libère d'abord toutes les dérivées d'entrée encore actives, puis la
compagne". Used: the entries active at the start of `unresolve`, in record order, then the companion;
`reject` if one release is not accepted or the companion is unknown (ghost lookup). The ghost record
is kept.

## B. Representation choices (no accepted program changes)

- Library state `PState = ⟨kern : S3, pools, nId, res⟩` outside `S3` (§38, §46); pool identity a
  counter `nId` (§9 ¶7 analogue); registry index `j` designates the pool of an operation.
- Ghost resolutions `Res` (pool, internal, companion, mode, entries tagged with slot and generation):
  auxiliary information creating no right (§38), read only by `unresolve` and the invariants.
- `AdminRight s pl := Active internal ∧ Arena.MetaRight s pl.entry` (reuses the arena's §36
  `MetaRight`: `HasRight Modify` on the place holding `internal`).
- §56 guard: `NewPoolPre.guard : Guard56 (liveInternals s pools :: others) internal`; `others` (the
  other registries of live administrations, e.g. arenas and stacks) is a parameter of each `newPool`
  step, as in `Arena.NewArenaStep`.
- Outcomes: `Outcome3 PState`; `fail` and `reject` carry no state, so "state unchanged" is by
  construction (§58).
- `resolveMany Observe` = companion derive + successive `Observe` derives (`DerivesPre`,
  `derivesEff`); `Modify` = companion derive + `split` (mapping R5).
- `freeSlot` kernel effect = the O12 effect function `endUseEff` on the slot place (§69 effect), not an
  `EndUseStep`.
- Handles are not stored as values (no value layer in `S3`); `allocSlot` writes `dst` (`write3Eff`)
  and `slotHandle` gives the handle.

## C. Clauses not represented (no state content)

- D.3 "apte à recevoir la représentation d'un handle" (Spec 4 / Spec 11): no sizes or types in `S3`
  (policy: omit and record). Mapping suggested a `HandleFits` parameter; not added (policy).
- D.1 "leur métadonnée abstraite est représentée en octets": refinement, out of scope.
- D.4 generation overflow, encapsulation (Spec 9), persistent handle cycles: outside the abstract model.
# Readings — datastack (DS-v1, non-normative; spec v0 §36, §38, §46, §47, §56, §58, Part XIV, §82)

Module: `formal/Ern/Lib/DataStack.lean` (namespace `Ern.Lib.DataStack`).
Machine-checked examples: section `Witness` of that module (`run_ok`, `reading_above`,
`reading_order`, all by `decide` on library-reachable states under `Access.Examples.K0`).

Source of the contract: the brief's obligation 6 (DS-v1). Spec v0 does not define it (Part XIV
preamble: "The contracts of `HandlePool` and `DataStack` belong to their library abstractions and
are not defined here"). Every entry: clause, reading used, alternative, example whose verdict
changes. "[draft]" = the reading of the draft (`formal/derivability_0.1`, `Lib/DataStack.lean`),
used per policy ("use the draft's reading if the draft matches one of the readings").

## Readings that change verdicts

**DS-R1 "a cell above m" [draft].** DS-v1: "rejects if an active authority derived from internal
covers a cell above m". Reading: the cells at positions `[m.top, top)` (`above`), those that
`rewind m` returns. Alternative A: any cell at position `≥ m.top`. Alternative B: the regions issued
after `m`. Example (`Witness.reading_above`, decided): after `rewind ⟨0,1,1⟩` (top 1) and the
program's `release(5)`, `derive(4, [3], Modify)` gives authority 8, active, derived from `internal`
4, on cell 3 (position 1 ≥ `m0.top` = 0, but ≥ current top). `rewind ⟨0,0,0⟩` is `ok` here; under
A it is rejected. Safety is unaffected: the next `push` over cell 3 is rejected by the effective
right (§43, §61.1). Under B, a block grown after `m` from a base below `m` blocks `rewind` on its
lower part too (draft `opsE4`; not re-run here).

**DS-R2 order of the dead/foreign-mark `fail` and of the right of §36 [draft].** §58: "static
preconditions are checked before dynamic availability, according to the operation's contract";
DS-v1 lists "fails on a dead or foreign mark" first and says nothing about §36. Reading: mark
liveness first (`fail`), then `AdminRight` (`reject`). Alternative: §36 first. Example
(`Witness.reading_order` (1)): a callee frame with no right on the stack value rewinds to the
removed mark `⟨0,1,1⟩`: `fail` here, `reject` under the alternative. Consequence: `mark_no_aba`
gives `fail` unconditionally.

**DS-R3 "foreign" mark.** Reading: a mark is live for stack `j` iff `m.stack = j ∧ m ∈ st.marks`
(`LiveMark`); the stack identity is checked explicitly although, under `MarksWF` (proved on every
library-reachable state), membership alone implies it. No verdict changes on reachable states.
`rewind` on a stack index that does not exist is `reject` (no stack value) [draft].

**DS-R4 `grow` with `extra = 0` [draft].** DS-v1 says nothing. Reading: `reject` ("grow" means a
larger size). Alternative: an in-place re-issue of the same region. Example
(`Witness.reading_order` (2)): `grow(0, 5, 0)` in `d9` is `reject`, while release, static checks,
in-place check, `split` and `store` of the same region are all `ok` (alternative: `ok`).

**DS-R5 `grow` of a live block that cannot extend in place: `fail`** (libs.md C10; DS-v1 "fail
otherwise"). The draft rejected it. Reading: the in-place check (`InPlace`: the block ends at the top
and `extra` cells follow) is the availability check of the derived issue (§77.4) and gives `fail`.
A `b` that is no block of the stack gives `reject`. Example (`Witness.run_ok`): `grow(0, 5, 1)` in
`d7`, where block 6 lies above block 5, is `fail`.

**DS-R6 order inside `grow`.** The derived issue's static checks (`IssueStatic`) cannot be read on
the state before the release of `b` (the destination still holds `b`, §77.2 "holding no active
authority"). Reading: block lookup and `0 < extra` (`reject`); `release(b)` (`reject` if refused);
`IssueStatic` on the released state (`reject`); `InPlace` (`fail`, the state unchanged); `split`;
`store`. Alternative: in-place `fail` before the release. Changes the verdict when `b` cannot be
released and the block is not in place (`reject` here, `fail` under the alternative).

**DS-R7 `push` without room: `fail` [draft].** DS-v1 says only that `push` uses the derived issue.
Reading: the `size` cells at the top must exist (`top + size ≤ |cells|`); otherwise `fail`
(availability, §77.4), checked after `IssueStatic` on the requested cells that exist. Alternative:
"region belongs to the administered storage" (§77.2, static) gives `reject`. Example
(`Witness.reading_order` (3)): `push(0, 3, 4)` on a stack of 2 cells is `fail`.

**DS-R8 `push` static checks are those of the derived issue (`Arena.IssueStatic`, §77.1, §77.2).**
Not the draft's restricted ones: an `Init` destination is not rejected (spec v0 §77.2, O8.2).
`push` of size 0 is accepted (issue of the empty region): the empty block blocks no `rewind`, and
`rewind` forgets it in the metadata while its authority stays active [draft DS-3].

## Readings that change no accepted program (representation)

- **R1 State.** `DState = ⟨kern, stacks, fresh⟩`, separate from `S3` (§38, §46); a stack is its
  registry index, stacks are never removed; `fresh` is a global counter (§9 "a monotonically
  increasing counter is one possible representation"). The arena registry is not in `DState`: the
  guard reads it through the parameter `others` (§56), as `Arena.NewArenaPre` reads stacks through
  its `others`.
- **R2 Available cells** = positions `≥ top` of the ordered cells (`Stack.entry.available =
  cells.drop top`); `push` and `grow` take cells at the top only and `rewind` returns exactly
  `above`, so this is a set of leaves as in §46.
- **R3 `rewind` kernel part [draft]:** the derived reset of Part XIV restricted to `above st m`:
  `split(internal, [above])` then `release` of the new authority. Plus an explicit §36 check
  (`AdminRight`: `internal` active and `MetaRight` on the stack value) before the split, like
  `IssueStatic.live/metaRight`. Under the stack invariants (internal a `Modify` authority held by
  the stack value whose footprint contains the cells) and I3, `ok` holds exactly when DS-v1's
  condition and §36 hold; this converse is **not proved** here.
- **R4 "removes m and every mark above it":** "above" = later in the ordered list;
  `marks := takeWhile (· ≠ m)`. Blocks with base `≥ m.top` are forgotten [draft].
- **R5 `newStack` preconditions [draft]:** `Arena.NewArenaBase` (§76.1–§76.3, §76.5 read for a
  stack) and `Guard56 (stackInternals :: others)`. DS-v1 says nothing about creation.
- **R6 `mark` [draft]:** no right required, `ok` on an existing stack (it changes metadata only,
  creates no right, §36), `reject` on a missing stack.
- **R7 `grow` destination [draft]:** the destination recorded for the block (`Blk.dst`), which may be
  `Moved` after a `transfer` of the block value; the new block is stored there.
- **R8 Library runs:** `DStep.kernel` admits any kernel step of non-administrative code.

# Report — handlepool (non-normative library instance, "HandlePool v0.4 annex")

File: `formal/Ern/Lib/HandlePool.lean` (new, untracked; module `Ern.Lib.HandlePool`, namespace
`Ern.Lib.HandlePool`; imports `Ern.MemoryModel.Arena` and `Ern.MemoryModel.Access.Preserve.EndFree`).
Nothing committed; no other file touched. Readings: `scratchpad/ref/readings/handlepool.md`.

## Status

- `lake build Ern.Lib.HandlePool`: success; `lake env lean` on the file prints nothing (no warning).
- `axcheck.sh Ern.Lib.HandlePool`: 580+ constants, `outside propext, Quot.sound: #[]` (no
  `Classical.choice`). No `sorry/admit/native_decide/axiom/noncomputable/set_option`; no Mathlib
  tactic; no line over 100 characters.
- Every declaration has a docstring citing a § clause; contract items cite "HandlePool v0.4 annex,
  D.k"; the module docstring and the contract definitions state "non-normative". No draft citation.
- Witnesses decided by `decide` (kernel-checked); `KInv ∧ KAux` of witness states via
  `Arena.KInvB.sound`.

## Definitions (clause → Lean)

- State (D.1; §38, §46, §47): `Slot`, `Pool`, `Handle`, ghost `Res`, `PState` (kernel + registry +
  `nId` + ghost resolutions), `PState.init`.
- §36 right: `AdminRight s pl := Active internal ∧ Arena.MetaRight s pl.entry` (Modify on the place

186	**P0. Spec v0 does not specify either contract.** §75: "The contracts of `HandlePool` and `DataStack` belong to their library abstractions and are not defined here." AGENTS.md: "`specs/` is normative and the only source of semantics." Annex D calls itself "non normative" and says "les résultats … concernent le modèle exploratoire …, **pas** automatiquement les règles corrigées". DS-v1 exists only in the brief. Every HandlePool/DataStack definition beyond §36/§37/§56/§58/§89 therefore encodes semantics from outside `specs/`. A decision is needed: either accept Annex D + brief obligation 5 and DS-v1 as the normative source for this formalization (and cite them), or add the contracts to `specs/`.
187	
188	**P1. Pool slot layout is under-determined, and the choice changes accepted programs.** D.1: "Les slots sont des sous-emplacements deux à deux disjoints, inclus dans `storage`". `newPool(storage, internal)` receives no slot description. The draft picks the direct children (`newPoolEff` HP:116). Example: storage `S = {a: {x, y}, b}`. "Slots = children" gives 2 slots `a, b`, so a third `allocSlot` gives `fail`. "Slots = leaves" gives 3 slots `x, y, b`, so the third gives `ok`. A storage that is a single leaf gives 0 slots under the draft, so every `allocSlot` gives `fail`.
189	
190	**P2. Outcome of `freeSlot` on a free slot whose generation matches.** D.3: "un slot déjà libre n'est pas rendu libérable par cette seule égalité" says it must not succeed, but not whether it gives `fail` or `reject`. Example (`pool_free_entry_handle` HZ:977): on a fresh pool, the fabricated handle `⟨0,0,0⟩` names free slot 0 of generation 0. The draft gives `ok`. The contract excludes `ok`, but `fail` (like `resolve`'s "slot … libre ⇒ fail") and `reject` are both possible readings.
191	
192	**P3. `resolve`: `reject` (no right) vs `fail` (bad handle) when both hold.** The right in D.2 ("exercice légal de `internal` au mode requis") includes the effective mode, which depends on the state. Spec v0 §77 orders the arena's analogous checks as availability `fail` (77.4) **before** the effective-right `reject` (77.5). Jalon3 H31a ("Deux `resolve Modify` simultanés, **quels que soient les handles** : le second `reject`") and the draft (HZ:590, `ResolveStep 0 ⟨0, 1, 7⟩ .modify h31 .reject` with a stale generation 7) put `reject` first. Example: with an active `Modify` companion, `resolve(stale h, Modify)` gives `reject` in the draft and `fail` under the §77 analogy. §58 defers to "the operation's contract", which does not settle it.
193	
194	**P4. Scope of "excluding `internal` and its ancestors" in `freeSlot`.**
195	- (a) D.3 lists only "aucune dépendance utilisable ne serait invalidée, aucune feuille n'est épinglée, et aucune autorité active ne couvre l'entrée hors `internal` et ses ancêtres"; the brief says "preconditions excluding internal and its ancestors". O12.3 includes "No place remaining usable after the effect depends on an authority held by `place`, **its root**, …". Example: a pool whose `internal` is the storage root (the `pb` setup HZ:565). If some usable place carries `internal` in `D` through `depend` (O5), the literal O12.3 rejects `freeSlot` (draft `EndUseAnchorOK` MM03:3989, `¬ IsRootOf`), although `freeSlot` leaves `internal` active. Whether the exemption also covers O12.3's root clause is not stated.
196	- (b) Kernel side, for the kernel mapper: in O12.2, "No active descendant over the leaves of `place` … is held outside the places dying with `place`, in a way that would prevent rights from returning", the descendant has no stated referent. The draft's literal reading (`EndUseAccessOK` MM03:3979: every active derived authority on an ending leaf) forbids `endUse` of any value stored inside an issued arena block while the block authority, held by the destination outside the block, is active. That authority is the one through which O12.1's `Modify` is exercised. Witness: `pool_freeSlot_derived_internal` HZ:925. It decides whether `freeSlot` can be a kernel `endUse` step (§2 item 8).
197	
198	**P5. D.3 contradicts itself when `dst` lies in the allocated slot.** "Le contenu du slot demeure `Uninit` … l'écriture du handle dans `dst` n'initialise pas le slot" holds only if `dst` lies outside the slot. Unlike O18.2 ("leaf `destination` is not in `region`"), `allocSlot` does not exclude it. Example: a frame with `Modify` on the pool value has `internal` exercisable (§43, holder chain), so it has `HasRight .modify q` for a free-slot leaf `q`. `allocSlot(pool, dst := q)` satisfies every D.3 precondition (usable leaf, not `Init`, no authority held), picks slot `q`, and writes the handle into it: the slot becomes `Init`.
199	
200	**P6. "Les entrées libres sont `Uninit`" (D.1) is not an invariant of the open model.** A frame with `Modify` on the pool value can `derive` from `internal` onto a free slot (O1) and `write3` it (O10). That is the same mechanism as the draft counterexample `pool_inv_not_preserved` HP:1830 (a derive from the companion onto a free entry). A later `allocSlot` then hands out an `Init` slot even if `newPool` required `Uninit` storage. D.4 assigns encapsulation to Spec 9. The property can be stated only as an `allocSlot`/`freeSlot` effect, not as a reachable-state theorem, unless Spec 9 encapsulation is modeled.
201	
202	**P7. DataStack "a cell above m" is undefined.** It could mean `[m.top, top)` (cells that `rewind` returns) or any index ≥ `m.top`. Example (draft `opsE8`, `case_rewind_reading` DSL:1013): after an intermediate `rewind`, an authority `9` derived from `internal` covers cell 3 above the current top. `rewind ⟨0,0,0⟩` is accepted by the draft; under the literal "covers a cell above m" it is rejected. Safety is the same either way, since the next `push` of cell 3 is rejected by the effective right (§43 case 3). A "region issued after m" reading (Derivability (f) 7) gives a third answer for grown blocks (`opsE4`).
203	
204	**P8. DataStack ordering of statics against `fail`.** §58 says statics come before dynamic availability "according to the operation's contract". DS-v1 (as quoted) does not order (i) `rewind`'s administrative right (§36) against the dead/foreign-mark `fail`, or (ii) `push`/`grow` statics against the no-room `fail`. §75 describes the derived issue as "split followed by store (after checking availability)", which suggests availability first. §77 puts statics first. Example: a callee with no right over the stack value (`opsZ` DSL:1029) calls `rewind` with a removed mark. The draft gives `fail`; statics first gives `reject`.
205	
206	**P9. DataStack `grow` details not covered by DS-v1 (as quoted):**
207	- `extra = 0`: the draft gives `reject` (DSL:221 `0 < extra`).
208	- whether `b` must be releasable (the draft checks `ReleasePre` statically);
209	- the destination after the block value has been transferred: the draft stores into the recorded `Blk.dst`, which may then be `Moved` and no longer the holder (Derivability (f)).
210	
211	**P10 (low). `resolveMany Observe` with invalid handles.** D.2 states the atomic `fail` ("toute identité invalide, génération périmée, entrée libre ou répétition de slot donne `fail` **atomique**") only in the `Modify` sentence. For `Observe`, it says only "sans `split` ni contrôle de distinction". The natural reading (an invalid handle gives an atomic `fail`) is not written down.
212	
213	No contradiction with the Charter was found. Charter §4.1 lists the five guarantees and §3.4 sends features to libraries; both are consistent with every item above.
214	
215	---
216	
217	## 5. Representation choices recommended (they change no accepted program)
218	
219	- **R1.** One library record `Lib` (arenas, pools, stacks, `nextPool`, `nextMark`, ghost `res`) beside `S3`, with a single function `liveInternals : Lib → S3 → List AuthorityId` for §56. This follows §38 and §56 ("Its physical representation and encapsulation of library registries remain outside the kernel").
220	- **R2.** Pool identity as a counter (`nId`), mark identity as a counter (`fresh`): §9 "A monotonically increasing counter is one possible representation".
221	- **R3.** A stack's identity is its registry index; stacks are never removed, so indices are never reused. `Mark = (stack, id, top)` as in the draft.
222	- **R4.** Ghost resolution registry `Res` (companion, mode, entries tagged with slot and generation), read only by `unresolve` and by the invariants. It is auxiliary information that creates no rights (§38 last sentence, applied to library state).
223	- **R5.** `resolveMany Modify` realized as `derive` companion + `split` on the entry footprints. With the distinctness check placed first, this accepts exactly the batches that successive `derive`s from the companion would accept, because entries are disjoint (`pool_entries_disjoint`).
224	- **R6.** Library operations as relations with `ok | fail | reject` (`POutcome`/`Out`), `fail` carrying the unchanged state. `allocSlot` is a relation over any free slot. Executable runners (`pexec`, `drun`) keep a deterministic choice (`firstFree`) and are proven to agree with the relation on every result they return (DESIGN.md, Representation).
225	- **R7.** Stack availability as the index `top`, with `available st := st.cells.drop st.top`. This is equivalent to an explicit leaf set (§46 `available: Set<Leaf>`) because `push` and `grow` take cells only at the top and `rewind` returns exactly `[m.top, top)`. A lemma stating that equivalence makes C5 literal.
226	- **R8.** Handle as `(poolId, slot index, gen)` with the slot index read as a position in `Pool.slots`; a slot index out of range never names an entry (`fail`).
227	- **R9.** `AdminRight` (§2 item 3) shared by arenas, pools and stacks, so one definition carries the §36 citation.
228	
229	I did not check that any build compiles: no Lean was run. Line numbers come from `git show formal/derivability_0.1:<path>`. The DS-v1 rows rest only on the brief's quoted summary.
230

# Task brief (verbatim obligations, as given by the user)

Normative hierarchy: Charter v0 highest (contradictions reported, never resolved); spec specs/ERN_Memory_Model_Specification_v0.md validated and frozen, cite by section; draft branches formal/* are material only (reuse when matching the spec, divergences resolved in favor of the spec and listed).
Layout (suggested): Ern/MemoryModel/Machine.lean (Part III), Ern/MemoryModel/Access/*.lean (Parts IV-XIII, XV-XVI), Ern/MemoryModel/Arena.lean (Part XIV: arenas as reference library abstraction; O17-O19 derived over O1-O16 plus metadata; ArenaInv and the §56 guard as abstraction contract), Ern/MemoryModel/Refinement.lean (§82), Ern/Lib/HandlePool.lean, Ern/Lib/DataStack.lean (non-normative), test modules imported by no model module. MM-01 (Part II) referenced, not a module.

Obligations (all mandatory):
1. Machine (Part III). Relations total and deterministic; interpreters calculable with static obligations and WF as proof arguments; agreement theorems both ways on their domain; admissible-state invariants preserved; P1-P4, no double free, frame lemmas, read-after-write on every included sub-range (§16).
2. Kernel (Parts IV-XIII). Every operation exactly as written, including §63.8 and §77 local self-blocking prevention, §65 store rules (derived authority, free leaf, arrival-state exercisability), §72 parameter-origin rule, §73 reanchoring to the first surviving active origin, §69/§70 end of use and free, pinning rules. Locals created by entering a frame are owned directly by the frame; alloc creates exactly one root. Theorems: preservation of WF3 ∧ Inv3 ∧ AnchorOrderHeld ∧ NoOrphan by every step; reachable invariant from S3.init statics under DDSound; exitFrame_no_dangling; call_params_effective_protected; effective_exclusive; init_only_by_writes, init_statics, and the global induction (every Init leaf of a reached state was declared or written); correspondence between Step and Reachable.
3. Arena (Part XIV). issue_as_kernel, reset_as_kernel (both directions, same arrival state on the kernel part), newArena_as_library (no safety property depends on the guard), arena_reuse_safe, ArenaInv preserved.
4. Refinement (§82). Repr including MM-02 WF; R1, R2, R4, R6 for every kernel operation and derived arena operation; simulation with parameters fixed once per run; freeSound_derived; pinned_address_stable; exclusive_bytes. Decisions to apply: declared disjointness is disjointness of leaves (byte disjointness follows from layout well-formedness); a pointer to an empty region has address = base of the effective anchor's allocation and that allocation as provenance; a region's pointer address is the lowest address among its non-empty leaves; a leaf receiving a reference has pointer size (stated hypothesis, classed types/ABI).
5. HandlePool (contract: v0.4 annex). Composite borrow (companion derived from internal over the whole storage, entries derived from the companion); resolveMany Observe by Observe derivations, distinctness only in Modify; allocSlot/freeSlot require a live pool and Modify on the pool value; newPool requires Uninit storage; freeSlot ends the entry content with endUse effects, preconditions excluding internal and its ancestors; PoolInv = entry disjointness + pool_no_stale_access + transition guarantee that freeSlot never succeeds on an entry covered by an active companion descendant. Theorems: pool_resolve_modify_exclusive, pool_no_stale_access, stale/other-pool/atomicity/distinctness, pool_freeSlot_ends_content under the Modify right.
6. DataStack (contract below, identifier DS-v1). Marks carry stack identity and a fresh mark identifier; the stack keeps the ordered list of live marks; rewind m fails on a dead or foreign mark, rejects if an active authority derived from internal covers a cell above m, otherwise returns those cells to available and removes m and every mark above it; push and grow use the derived issue; grow is in place only (same base, extension into the space directly after the block, fail otherwise). Theorems: rewind_rejects_live_above, mark_no_aba (for every removed mark), rewind_keeps_older_marks, grow_same_base, grow_keeps_prefix_init, grow_keeps_prefix_bytes through the refinement.
7. Corpora. Encode MM2-H (first execution), MM3-H and MM23-H (replay) from the attached material, plus new cases: §63.8 and §77 self-blocking (reject, with twins), §56 guard, corrected HandlePool, DataStack (including ABA and a multi-stack frame scenario), W1-W3. Each case: reached state from the initial state, expected verdict from its source, positive twin for each rejection, class. MM23-H15 and H16 must now pass. Section J of MM3-H stays unencoded and classified. No case is corrected or bypassed.

Docstrings: model modules: every def/theorem cites the specification clause it formalizes. Library modules: cite the applicable spec clauses (§36, §56, ...) and the local contract identifier (HandlePool v0.4 annex, DS-v1), stated as non-normative.
Exclusions: instrumented checked variants; duplicate _pre statements; references to draft reports; concurrency beyond the stat boundary; syntax.
Rules: zero sorry; #print axioms at most {propext, Quot.sound} on every constant (checked by script); no noncomputable; lake build without warnings; nothing invented - a clause that cannot be formalized as written is reported, not interpreted; no statement weakened relative to its clause; adversarial review rounds, every finding re-checked by a refuter.
Opening the PR: only if every mandatory obligation is proved and every expected/obtained mismatch resolved; otherwise commit on the branch, do not push, do not open the PR, end with a blocking report (each unproved obligation or mismatch classified as specification defect, module defect or case defect, with its counterexample). Never present a partial formalization as conforming.

## 36. Shared Mutation and Internal Administration

An abstraction may keep its metadata in `SharedMutable` storage and modify it through `writeShared` to the extent permitted by the applicable rights and contracts. **Shared mutation of metadata does not, however, grant the right to create, recycle, or terminate exclusive authority over the administered storage.** Such operations require `internal` to be exercisable in `Modify` mode from the value administering the storage.

For every administrative abstraction, including arenas, `HandlePool`, and `DataStack`, **`MetaRight` requires `Modify` exercisable on the administering value**. The `writeShared` branch alone is insufficient. Operations issuing, recycling, ending, or invalidating regions must preserve active authorities and dependencies. Allocation through administration shared among simultaneous holders, under an interface not providing such exclusive exercise, cannot be expressed in safe code with only these sequential operations: any synchronized implementation of it belongs to Spec 2. These abstractions remain libraries and add no rights to the kernel.

## 37. Dependent Values and Persistent References

When a value depends on the validity of other storage, that dependency must be carried by an explicit mechanism. In particular, this model retains:

- joint ownership or legal transfer of the resource;
- **non-escaping** dependent values, governed by `depend`, `store`, `AnchorOrder`, and end-of-use operations; they may survive a call if their anchors come from still-valid caller resources;
- library handles checked for identity and generation upon resolution, which are not authorities by themselves;
- validity durations bound to a frame or context, without a universal system of first-class lifetimes;
- safe abstractions encapsulating, when necessary, unsafe operations and proofs of their obligations.

**Not adopted as a universal ERN mechanism:** a first-class persistent reference subject to general lifetime constraints at the type-system level. The above mechanisms are complementary; neither a handle nor a temporary access guarantees the perpetual validity of its target resource on its own.

## 38. Machine State

The access discipline is based on the finite state

\[ S_3=(F,P,I,A,D) \]

where `F` represents the frame stack, `P` the places, `I` their initialization, `A` the authorities, and `D` the validity anchors. Administrative states of arenas and other library abstractions are separate from `S₃`. The external contract `K` is a separate parameter. The internal representation may carry auxiliary information that creates no new rights.

## 43. Effective Rights and Exercise of Authorities

For an authority `a` and a leaf `l`, `effective(s,a,l)` is derived from the active descendants of `a` whose footprint contains `l`:

1. if `a` is inactive or does not cover `l`, its effective mode is absent;
2. if no active descendant covers `l`, the effective mode is the own mode of `a`;
3. if an active descendant with own mode `Modify` covers `l`, the effective mode of `a` is absent;
4. otherwise, when the covering active descendants are `Observe`, the effective mode of `a` on `l` is `Observe`.

The effect is **local to each leaf**: after splitting a region, the origin may retain effective `Modify` over undistributed leaves.

Requested modes are ordered `Observe ≤ Modify`. `ExercisableAt(s,a,m)` means:

- `a` is active and its own mode permits `m`;
- either `a` is held by the current frame;
- or `a` is held by a place `p`, and the current frame has, over **all** leaves of `p`, an authority itself exercisable in mode `m` with sufficient effective mode.

The latter clause is recursive along the holder chain. Thus, being active or covering a leaf does not automatically make an authority exercisable. `HasRight(s,m,p)` means the current frame has exercise in mode `m` and sufficient effective mode **over every leaf in `p`'s footprint**. Every operation requires the modes it actually needs; an authority's own mode alone is insufficient.

## 46. Arenas as Library Administration States

Each entry belongs to the library's abstract state, **separate from kernel state `S₃`**. It has the following fields:

```text
ArenaEntry {
    storage: PlaceId
    internal: AuthorityId
    available: Set<Leaf>
    issued: Set<(Region, AuthorityId)>
}
```

A region is **available if and only if each of its leaves belongs to `available`**; the empty region is always available. Issuance removes the leaves of the issued region from `available`. Reset restores all leaves of the administered storage to that set. The registry and its updates belong to the abstraction contract and create no kernel permissions.

The arena is **live** if `internal` is active. The **arena value** is the place holding `internal`, distinct from the possible owner of `storage`. Administered storage may be local, static, allocated, or issued by another arena, under `newArena` preconditions and applicable invariants. `available` and `issued` remain **in the library's arena entry**.

## 47. Initial State

The kernel's initial state contains only base frame 0 and the declared static storage. Every static leaf has its declared initial state, `Init` or `Uninit`. The roots of static places directly owned by frame 0 have a root `Modify` authority held by that frame; a static may also be owned by another static, in which case its root authority is held by the latter. The initial state invents no dynamic allocation, derived authority, or implicit anchor. The initial arena registry belongs to library state and is empty. The initial frame does not exit.

## 48. External Parametric Contract
## 55. ArenaInv — Invariant of the Arena Abstraction

`ArenaInv` is an invariant of the **library contract**, not an additional predicate of kernel state. For every live arena:

- `storage` designates an existing, usable place; the footprint of `internal` is exactly the footprint of `storage`;
- `internal` is active, with own mode `Modify`, held by the arena value;
- available leaves and issued regions belong to the administered storage;
- two still-active issuances have disjoint regions; no leaf of a still-issued region simultaneously belongs to `available`;
- every still-issued block authority is a derivative of `internal` complying with exclusivity and validity rules;
- anchor and ownership restrictions are respected.

Arena entries do not, by themselves, constitute an additional storage owner. Two live arenas may cover common leaves when their `internal` authorities are distinct and their effective rights are compatible; no **global** disjointness of arena footprints is imposed.

## 56. Uniqueness of Live Administration

**An authority identity may serve as `internal` for at most one live administrative abstraction**, whether an arena, `HandlePool`, `DataStack`, or another library administrative instance. Before registering a new abstraction, its creation operation must jointly check the absence of that identity from **all relevant registries of live administrations**. Uniqueness concerns the identity of the `internal` authority, not merely possible overlap of footprints: abstractions with distinct `internal` identities are not forbidden merely because their footprints overlap. Library contracts must make the information required for this guard available to the creation operation; checking only an abstraction's own registry is insufficient.

**This guard is not a condition for any safety property in Section 57.** The effective right (Section 43, case 3) already prohibits a second issuance over leaves covered by an active block derived from the same authority. Rather, the guard preserves the **abstraction contract**: without it, simultaneous administration of the same `internal` could cause `reject` instead of `fail`, or reissue a previously released block that the first administration still considers unavailable. It creates neither permissions nor allocations and introduces no general detection of authority cycles. Its physical representation and encapsulation of library registries remain outside the kernel.

## 57. Main Invariant

\[
Inv3 = I1 \land I2 \land I3 \land I4 \land AnchorOrder \land NoDangling
\]

On states reachable from `S3.init statics` under `DDSound(K)`, the kernel guarantees:

\[
WF3 \land Inv3 \land AnchorOrderHeld \land NoOrphan
\]

`ArenaInv` (Section 55) belongs to the library abstraction: it is not included in this main kernel invariant.

I5, associated with pinned storage, remains a **specialized obligation** of `K.Pinned`, not a clause automatically implied by sequential accesses alone. This property is required for reachable states under the declared assumptions. Its correspondence with allocations and bytes requires the refinement defined below.

# VIII. Definition of Transitions and Management of Authorities

The following operations are abstract transition rules. They distinguish rejection by the discipline, defined failure, and a permitted transition.

## 58. Transition Outcomes

Every operation has a conceptual outcome among:

```text
Outcome3 = ok(new_state) | reject | fail
```

`reject` means that the static discipline does not permit the step; it is neither an implicit runtime trap nor `ub` in the elementary memory machine. `fail` is a **defined failure** leaving the state unchanged; **only `alloc` may produce it in the O1–O16 kernel**. Other kernel operations produce `ok` or `reject`. Library-abstraction operations, including `issue` (§77), may define their own `fail` cases. Where such failure is provided, static preconditions are checked before dynamic availability, according to the operation's contract.

An `ok` transition must satisfy its preconditions, apply exactly its prescribed effects, and preserve the relevant invariants. No transition fabricates a permission to make its conclusion true. Holder and anchor changes are evaluated in the **resulting state** when a rule explicitly so provides.

## 59. Implicit Preservation of Modes and Anchors

## 61. O2 — Splitting Authorities

**Preconditions**

1. `source` is active and exercisable by the current frame with sufficient modification rights over the relevant leaves.
2. Each region lies within the available, effectively modifiable footprint of the source.
3. Regions are pairwise disjoint under structural composition or contract `K.DeclaredDisjoint`, subject to obligation `DDSound(K)`; no exclusive right already distributed is overlapped.
4. Creation of the derivatives respects origins, conservation I1/I2, and validity obligations.

**`ok` effect:** An active derived `Modify` authority held by the current frame is created for each region. `source` remains active; its effective modification capability disappears only over distributed leaves and remains on undistributed leaves. Authorities are split logically: `split` performs no physical allocation. **Other outcome:** `reject`.

An unjustified declaration of disjointness may invalidate the proof: without `DDSound`, an accepted `split` may violate I1. Constructing zero-sized subregions is not identified with an allocation of the elementary memory machine; the case of an empty shape in `alloc` is distinct.

## 62. O3 — End of a Derived Borrow

**Preconditions**

1. `authority` is active **and derived**: an authority with no origin is rejected.
2. It is held by the current frame, or by a place `p` on which the current frame has exercisable `Modify`.
3. No active descendant of the authority prevents its release; no other still-usable value may lose a required anchor.
4. If the authority is stored in its holding place, that place is exempted from the check “this authority still appears among the anchors” **only because the effect removes that anchor at the same time**. An anchor with the same identity attached by `depend` to another usable place continues to block the step.
5. Applicable abstraction contracts remain satisfied.

**`ok` effect:** The authority becomes inactive and can no longer be exercised. It is removed from its holding place's anchors when stored there. Effective modes of its origins are recomputed, allowing unblocked rights to return. There is no implicit deallocation. **Other outcome:** `reject`.

# IX. Transfer, Dependencies, and Storage of Rights
## 69. O12 — Logical End of a Value's Use

**Preconditions**

1. `place` is usable and the current frame has exercisable `Modify` over it.
2. No active descendant over the leaves of `place` **or storage that dies with it** is held outside the places dying with `place`, in a way that would prevent rights from returning or being invalidated.
3. No place **remaining usable after the effect** depends on an authority held by `place`, its root, or an authority that would become inactive when an owned holder dies.
4. **No leaf whose use ends, including transitively owned storage, is pinned**, either statically (`K.Pinned`) or dynamically (`pin`). A dynamic pinning obligation must be legally removed by `unpin` before this step.

**`ok` effect:** The leaves of value `place` become `Uninit`; `place` **remains usable as a place** and may legally be reinitialized. Authorities held by `place` and dead substorages are released; dependencies of the ended value are removed; transitively owned places that cease to live are marked dead. The operation does not automatically trigger physical deallocation in the elementary memory machine: an unfreed allocation may constitute a leak, which this guarantee does not prohibit. **Other outcome:** `reject`.

## 70. O13 — Release of an Owned Storage Unit

**Preconditions**

1. `place` is a **root of storage owned by a value** (`OwnedRoot`), not an ordinary local directly owned by a frame and not part of an aggregate.
2. `K.Deallocable(place)` is established, and `K.FreeCompat(place,auth)` justifies deallocation authority `auth`; this identifier is opaque to the authority kernel.
3. The current frame has exercisable `Modify`; no active derivative over the footprint being freed is held outside holders that die; no surviving place is anchored to an authority of the released region or of its dead holders.
4. No leaf of the released unit is statically or dynamically pinned. Ending external use does not silently turn a still-pinned leaf into a releasable unit.

**`ok` effect:** `place` and the storage that ceases to live are marked dead; authorities of those regions, including their corresponding roots, become inactive, as do authorities whose holders die. Surviving dependencies must remain valid. Every realization of `free` must satisfy the corresponding deallocation relation of the elementary memory machine (Part III). **Other outcome:** `reject`.

## 71. O14 — Allocation of a New Storage Root
## 75. O16 — Removal of Dynamic Pinning

**Preconditions:** `place` is usable, the current frame has exercisable `Modify`, and contract `K.ExternalDone(place)` attests that all relevant external use has ended.

**`ok` effect:** The corresponding dynamic pinning obligation ends, without itself modifying values, their initialization, or their access authorities. Static obligations are not removed by this operation. **Other outcome:** `reject`.

**Associated static rule (`StaticPinnedBottom`):** Statics designated by `K.Pinned` must be places **directly** owned by the **base frame**, not merely transitively owned by a static value. This restriction ensures that they do not die when an intermediate frame exits.

# XIV. Arenas and Collective Invalidation — Reference Abstraction

An arena is a **library abstraction**, not a memory-kernel primitive. Operations O17 through O19 are **derived** from operations O1 through O16 and abstraction-specific metadata: `newArena` registers an administration without modifying the kernel; `issue` performs `split` followed by `store` (after checking availability); `reset` performs a `Modify` derivation over all storage—through `derive` or `split`—then `release`, before restoring availability. Their contract below is **normative for the standard-library arena** until Spec 10 takes responsibility for it. It authorizes neither new permissions nor an additional access machine. Arena entries (Section 46) constitute the abstract state of this administration; the guard in Section 56 belongs to its consistency contract. The contracts of `HandlePool` and `DataStack` belong to their library abstractions and are not defined here.

## 76. O17 — Creation of an Administered Arena

**Preconditions**

1. `storage` is an existing, usable place under exercisable `Modify` by the current frame. It may be local, static, allocated, or a block issued by a previous arena.
2. `internal` is explicitly named by the caller, exists, is active, has own mode `Modify`, and `ExercisableAt(s,internal,Modify)` holds.
3. `internal` is **held by a place**: that place is the arena value; `footprint(internal) = footprint(storage)`.
4. **Unified administration guard (Section 56):** no **live** administrative abstraction, whether an arena or a library instance such as a handle pool, already uses this `internal` identity. The relevant registries of library administrations are consulted before registration. Two distinct identities may cover common leaves: this is not in itself grounds for rejection.
5. All leaves of the arena value holding `internal` are already `Init`; construction does not initialize them implicitly.
6. Dependency, holder, storage, and administration relations respect `WF3`, I1, `AnchorOrder`, `AnchorOrderHeld`, and the expected arena invariants.

**`ok` effect:** A live entry `{storage, internal, available, issued}` is added; the initial `available` set represents the administered storage, and `issued` is initially empty. Registering the entry fabricates no place, access right, or `Init` state. **Other outcome:** `reject`.

The identity of `internal`, not the index of `storage`, is the key to preventing duplication of live administrations. No global constraint requires footprints of live arenas to be pairwise disjoint.

## 77. O18 — Issuing an Arena Block

**Static preconditions**

1. The `arena` entry exists and is live; `internal` is active. `MetaRight` requires exercisable `Modify` over the arena value holding `internal` (Section 36). Mutation of metadata through `writeShared` alone does not satisfy this condition.
2. `region` belongs to the administered storage; `destination` is a usable **leaf** holding no active authority; the destination can legally receive the block value in mode `Modify`. The fact that `destination` is already `Init` is not in itself grounds for rejection, in accordance with O8.2.
   **Local self-blocking prevention: leaf `destination` is not in `region`, including when the region is declared available.** This condition is static and is checked before an availability `fail`.
3. Applicable **static** validity and non-escape restrictions for the destination are satisfied. The `AnchorOrder` check depending on the new anchor is performed on the **simulated resulting state**, after the availability check described in point 4; it cannot turn an unavailable issuance (`fail`) into `reject`.

**Availability and exercisability checks**

4. If static conditions hold but **at least one leaf of `region` does not belong to `available`**, the operation produces **`fail` and leaves the entire state unchanged**. The empty region is always available. An unavailable region does not permit a prior static rejection to be bypassed.
5. If the region is available, the effective mode of `internal` on that region must permit `Modify`; otherwise the outcome is `reject`.
6. The simulated result must satisfy `AnchorOrderHeld` **in the resulting state**; moreover, **in that resulting state, `destination` must remain under exercisable `Modify` by the current frame**, in accordance with O8.5. Issuance into a value with a longer lifetime than a local anchor is not made valid merely by storing it in the caller.

**`ok` effect:** A block authority of fresh identity, derived from `internal` and of mode `Modify`, is issued for the region; it is held by `destination`, which receives the corresponding anchor. The leaves of the region leave `available`, and the issuance is added to `issued` with its authority. **Only leaf `destination` becomes `Init`**; no other leaf of the arena value changes initialization. Previous issuances remain intact and valid. Issuance does not automatically install anchors on third-party values: they must use their lawful dependency mechanisms.

**Outcomes:** `ok`, `fail` (region unavailable after static validation), `reject` (static rule, effective right, or anchoring not satisfied). The destination may be a leaf of the arena value itself: its initialization then constitutes **an explicit write to that destination**, not implicit initialization of the entire arena value's metadata.

## 78. O19 — Collective Arena Reset

**Preconditions**

1. The entry exists and is live. **`MetaRight(s,arena)` requires exercisable `Modify` over the arena value**, in accordance with Section 36. `writeShared` over metadata alone, even when legal, does not replace such exercise. `internal` and the arena's other restrictions remain valid.
2. **No active authority derived from `internal` covers a leaf of the administered storage.** A derived authority with an empty footprint does not, by itself, block `reset`.
3. No still-usable place depends, directly or transitively, on an anchor in the **strict origin subtree of `internal`** (`internal` itself is excluded). Under precondition 2 and invariant I3, this condition follows from the absence of active descendants covering the storage, and remains explicit in the abstraction contract. Validity obligations of other nested arenas remain satisfied.

**`ok` effect:** All **leaves** of the administered storage become available again, and the issuance list is cleared under the arena contract. No still-active derived authority covering those leaves may remain, by precondition 2; an empty-footprint derivative may remain active without designating any recycled leaf. **No leaf is made `Init` by `reset`**, including in the arena value. **Other outcome:** `reject`.

Safe reuse after `reset` requires that previous issuances **covering recycled leaves**, and the dependencies on which their validity rests, have effectively ceased preventing their reuse. Any active empty-footprint derivatives cover none of those leaves. A historically issued region does not remain permanently unavailable solely for that reason.

# XV. Transitive Dependencies, Returns, and Value Behavior
## 82. Representation Relation and Concrete Obligations

1. **Places and bytes:** relate `P`, `footprint` leaves, their ownership, and their parts to the storage units, offsets, ranges, identities, and alignment constraints of the elementary memory machine; establish actual disjointness for `DeclaredDisjoint` declarations.
2. **Authorities and operations:** connect effective modes and `ExercisableAt` to concrete read, write, and pointer-validity conditions; show that safe access governed by Parts VI through XV satisfies the obligations of Part III, without conflating ownership and binary representation.
3. **Initialization:** relate `Uninit`, `Init`, and `Moved` to concrete values and representations; an authority `store` must correspond to writing an actual reference into **a single logical leaf** with an appropriate representation.
4. **Allocation and deallocation:** relate `alloc` / `free` to `AllocStep` / `DeallocStep`, justify `Satisfiable`, `Deallocable`, and `FreeCompat`, as well as the zero-physical-size case.
5. **Lifetimes:** relate `endUse`, `exitFrame`, `NoDangling`, dependencies, and death markers to the validity effects on actual storage.
6. **Pinning and static storage:** prove compatibility of permitted moves and pinned-address restrictions; specify the physical obligations of statics and external use. Hardware-specific MMIO semantics remain outside the sequential kernel.
7. **Arenas:** show that the library abstraction's derived operations and metadata, distinct from `S₃`, can be realized by operations O1–O16; relate issued regions and local/static/allocated storage to the elementary memory machine without reintroducing access after invalidation.
8. **`noalias`:** infer no pointer-lowering property from abstract invariants alone; memory justification is established here and the translation choices at Spec 13 level.

# XVIII. Examples of Semantic Behavior
## 86. Arena, Active Views, and Reset

Two disjoint issued regions may be used simultaneously with valid derived rights. `reset` is rejected while an issuance or active dependency would make recycling unsafe; after a legal end of use for all the relevant blocks, the region may be reissued. Reissuance does not permit reading a former logical value without the required initialization.

## 87. Pinning an In-Place Value

A pinned in-place leaf cannot be physically moved by `transfer`. If only an allocation owned by a value is pinned, transfer of that value may remain valid when the other conditions hold, because the owned allocation is not physically moved.

## 88. Local Self-Blocking and Indirect Cycles

An authority stored by `transfer` in a place that would then become its new holder cannot cover any leaf of that place. Likewise, `issue` cannot issue into a leaf belonging to the issued region, **or into a destination that would no longer be exercisable in `Modify` in the resulting state** (O8.5). These restrictions do not promise general freedom from authority cycles: indirect blocking compatible with safety may remain.

## 89. Handles and Persistent References

In a generation-based pool library abstraction, a handle may contain a logical pool identity, an entry identifier, and a generation. This handle is not, by itself, an access right. Safe resolution temporarily supplies authority when the pool and entry are valid; a stale identity or generation leads to defined failure. These conditions belong to the safe abstraction's contract and do not modify the authority-discipline kernel.

## 90. Global and Called Frame
